A DOG'S PERFECT CHRISTMAS officially releases tomorrow, November 4, on Netflix, bringing a brand new heartwarming holiday movie starring Dennis Quaid and Mary Steenburgen.

Based on the novel by W. Bruce Cameron, the bestselling author behind A DOG'S PURPOSE, the film follows a family whose Christmas plans fall apart after an unexpected medical emergency changes everything.

At the center of the story is Winstead, a loyal basset hound who tries to bring his struggling family back together before Christmas Eve, proving that sometimes the smallest members of a household can make the biggest difference.

The movie also stars Milo Ventimiglia, Jennifer Tilly, and Brooke Lena Johnson, with Thomas Haden Church providing the voice of Winstead. It marks another emotional dog-centered story from the author who brought audiences A DOG'S PURPOSE and A DOG'S JOURNEY.

Christmas movies are officially making their way back to Netflix, and A DOG'S PERFECT CHRISTMAS looks ready to deliver everything that makes the holidays special. Family, second chances, a little Christmas magic, and one very good dog holding everything together.

Netflix is once again testing a major redesign for its TV app. This new layout moves the main navigation menu back to the left-hand side of the screen, just months after the streamer rolled out a top-bar design globally. 

Beyond the sidebar, the test includes a layout that fits more titles on your screen at once, making it easier to scan through your watchlist. Video previews have also been moved to the top of the screen to free up space. This is currently only a test for select accounts, but it hints at where the Netflix experience is heading next.

“Good Morning America” anchor Robin Roberts says it “stings” to hear the words “fake news” amid Donald Trump’s attacks on the media.

"Think about if a world leader, a leader of your country, ripped your profession apart and made the public mistrust you. It hurts because we know how hard we work. We know how important our jobs are, and it stings. It stings when you hear the words 'fake news,' and they’re trying to undermine what we’re doing."

George Stephanopoulos adds: "I think our audience trusts us implicitly. That’s why they watch every day. I don’t want to overstate it, but people watch us in a different way. They watch us as they’re getting ready for their day, as they’re getting their family ready for their day. It’s a very intimate relationship, almost like we’re family. Now, more broadly, it’s a huge challenge. We’ve seen more than a decade of attacks on the media and people calling us into question."

“I don’t want to live with the regret, but I can tell you that I passed on ‘Ted’ and I’ve never had this experience where I laughed so hard reading a script. I literally took it to dinner and was reading parts of it out to my friends at dinner. And then I just got too clever by half. I don’t know what I was thinking. I was like, ‘Well, maybe the teddy bear’s actually the best part.’

So I overthought it and I talked myself out of it. And because it shot in Boston, it would’ve been a chance for me to be home — my father’s passed away now, and I look back and I go, ‘Man, that would’ve been six months back [home].’” (via GQ)

नेपालमा गैरकानुनी रूपमा बस्ने, काम गर्ने तथा विभिन्न आपराधिक गतिविधिमा संलग्न भएको अभियोगमा बाङ्ग्लादेशी नागरिकको पक्राउ र निष्कासन बढ्दै गएको छ। सरकारी तथ्याङ्कअनुसार चिनियाँ नागरिकपछि नेपालबाट सबैभन्दा धेरै निष्कासन हुने विदेशी नागरिकमा बाङ्ग्लादेशी छन्।

बीबीसी नेपालीका अनुसार पछिल्लो १० महिनामा ८६ जना बाङ्ग्लादेशी नागरिकलाई नेपालबाट निष्कासन गरिएको छ। पछिल्लो साउनदेखि असोजसम्मको चार महिनामा मात्रै ५१ जना निष्कासनमा परेका छन्। हाल अध्यागमन विभागको हिरासतमा १८ जना बाङ्ग्लादेशी नागरिक छन्।

कार्तिक १६ गते काठमाडौंका विभिन्न स्थानबाट चार बाङ्ग्लादेशी र एक भारतीय नागरिक पक्राउ परेका थिए। उनीहरूलाई थप अनुसन्धानका लागि अध्यागमन विभागमा बुझाइएको छ। यसअघि पनि अवैध रूपमा बसोबास गरेको, अनुमतिबिना काम गरेको र शङ्कास्पद गतिविधिमा संलग्न भएको अभियोगमा बाङ्ग्लादेशी नागरिक पक्राउ परेका थिए।

प्रहरीका अनुसार केही नागरिक पर्यटक भिसामा नेपाल आएर काम गर्ने, भिसाको म्याद सकिएपछि पनि बस्ने वा अवैध बाटोबाट प्रवेश गर्ने गरेको पाइएको छ। अनलाइन ठगीलगायत आपराधिक गतिविधिमा संलग्न भएको आशङ्कामा समेत अनुसन्धान भइरहेको अधिकारीहरूले बताएका छन्।

प्रहरीले दिएको तथ्याङ्कअनुसार पछिल्लो एक वर्षमा हवाई मार्गबाट १ लाख १७ हजार ६८२ बाङ्ग्लादेशी नागरिक नेपाल आएका वा फर्किएका छन्। तीमध्ये ५८ हजार ८७९ जना नेपाल भित्रिएका र ५८ हजार ८०३ जना फर्किएका छन्।

अध्यागमन विभागले भिसा उल्लङ्घन गर्नेहरूबाट आवश्यक शुल्क र जरिवाना असुल गरी केही वर्ष नेपाल प्रवेशमा रोक लगाएर निष्कासन गर्ने गरेको जनाएको छ। आपराधिक गतिविधिमा संलग्न भएको पुष्टि भएमा भने सम्बन्धित कानुनअनुसार कारबाही हुने अधिकारीहरूको भनाइ छ।

राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा)का सभापति रवि लामिछानेले पार्टीभित्र बढ्दै गएको अहङ्कार, अवसरवादी चरित्र र आन्तरिक ईर्ष्या त्याग्न नेता तथा कार्यकर्तालाई निर्देशन दिएका छन्।

शुक्रबार चितवनमा आयोजित पार्टीको आन्तरिक प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै लामिछानेले जनताले दिएको मतलाई अहङ्कारमा बदल्न नहुने बताए। पार्टीले सफलता हासिल गरेपछि केही नेता–कार्यकर्तामा घमण्ड बढेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले जनताको सेवक भएर काम गर्न आग्रह गरे।

उनले वडाध्यक्षको चुनाव लड्न नचाहने तर एकैपटक मेयर र सांसद बन्न खोज्ने प्रवृत्तिप्रति असन्तुष्टि जनाए। शक्तिको आडमा प्रहरी तथा प्रशासनलाई दबाब दिने राजनीति रास्वपाको नभएको पनि उनले स्पष्ट पारे।

आगामी निर्वाचनमा उम्मेदवार छनोट पार्टीको विधि र आन्तरिक निर्वाचन प्रणालीबाटै हुने भन्दै उनले भनसुन वा नेतासँगको निकटताका आधारमा टिकट नपाइने बताए। टिकट नपाएको भन्दै पार्टीलाई धोका दिने वा विपक्षीसँग मिल्ने प्रवृत्ति स्वीकार्य नहुने उनको भनाइ थियो।

लामिछानेले पार्टीको एकता, अनुशासन र पारदर्शितालाई मुख्य शक्ति मान्दै सबै नेता–कार्यकर्तालाई जिम्मेवार भएर अघि बढ्न आग्रह गरेका छन्।

काठमाडौंको सिंहदरबारभित्र पूर्वाधार मन्त्री सुनिल लम्सालका यातायात विज्ञ सल्लाहकार अनुकुल निधिको गाडीले राष्ट्रिय सभा सांसद राजेन्द्रलक्ष्मी गैरेलाई ठक्कर दिएको छ।

सांसद गैरेका अनुसार शुक्रबार पूर्वाधार मन्त्रालयअगाडिको जेब्रा क्रसिङबाट बाटो काट्ने क्रममा उनलाई गाडीले ठक्कर दिएर लडाएको हो। आफूले हात दिएर बाटो काटिरहेको भए पनि गाडीले ठक्कर दिएको उनले बताएकी छन्।

घटनामा बाहिरी चोट नदेखिए पनि शरीरमा दुखाइ भइरहेको गैरेको भनाइ छ। उनले घटनाबारे राष्ट्रिय सभा अध्यक्ष नारायणप्रसाद दाहाललाई समेत जानकारी गराएकी छन्।

पाल्पाकी गैरे नेकपाबाट राष्ट्रिय सभा सदस्य हुन्।

अर्थमन्त्री डा. स्वर्णिम वाग्लेले सरकारले साढे सातदेखि आठ महिनाको अवधिमा गरेका काममा कसैले औँला ठड्याउन नसकेको दाबी गरेका छन्। उनले यही गतिमा साढे चार वर्ष सरकार चलाएर आगामी चुनावमा अझ ठूलो शक्तिका रूपमा फर्किने बताएका छन्।

नेपाल इन्फ्रास्ट्रक्चर समिटसम्बन्धी कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै वाग्लेले सरकारले भ्रष्टतन्त्रको सफाइ गर्ने र विगतदेखि कायम राजनीतिक तथा प्रशासनिक अभ्यासमा परिवर्तन ल्याउने दाबी गरे। जुद्धशमशेरपछि कुनै सरकारले पाँच वर्ष पूरा नगरेको उल्लेख गर्दै उनले यसपटक त्यो क्रम तोड्ने बताए।

वाग्लेका अनुसार सरकारले अहिले १६६ वटा ऐनमाथि काम गरिरहेको छ। तीमध्ये ५९ वटा ऐनलाई एउटै प्याकेजमा अघि बढाउने तयारी छ। साथै, आठदेखि १० वटा ठूला पूर्वाधार आयोजना एकैपटक अघि बढाउने सरकारको योजना रहेको उनले जानकारी दिए।

उनले विकासमा निजी क्षेत्रको सहभागिता बढाउने, निजी पुँजी परिचालन गर्ने र वैकल्पिक विकास वित्तसम्बन्धी व्यवस्था कार्यान्वयनमा लैजाने बताए। बाढीपहिरोजस्ता चुनौतीका बाबजुद राजस्व संकलनको गति राम्रो रहेको उल्लेख गर्दै वाग्लेले यसलाई सरकारको सुशासन प्रयासको सकारात्मक परिणामका रूपमा व्याख्या गरे।

Australia Offers Two-Year Training Visa for Foreigners Without Student Visa

Australia's Training Visa (Subclass 407) allows eligible foreign nationals to undertake supervised workplace training and professional development for up to two years without enrolling in a traditional academic programme.

The visa is designed for people seeking to improve their professional skills, gain practical experience or acquire qualifications relevant to their careers. Applicants must have an approved Australian sponsor and meet English-language, health and other immigration requirements.

However, the visa is not a general work permit and is intended specifically for structured occupational training. Applicants must meet all eligibility conditions before applying.

Disturbing Details Emerge in Mamta Kafle Case: Husband Describes Dismembering Her Body

VIRGINIA, USA: In a shocking development in the disappearance and suspected murder case of Nepali nurse Mamta Kafle Bhatt, her husband, Naresh Bhatt, has admitted in court that he dismembered her body after finding her dead inside their bedroom.

During testimony at his murder trial on Thursday, Naresh told the court that he discovered Mamta lying unresponsive on the bedroom floor on the morning of July 30, 2024. He claimed that after finding her, he attempted to check whether she was alive and tried performing life-saving measures, including CPR.

According to his testimony, he noticed vomit around Mamta's mouth and on the bedroom floor. He described the substance as containing blood, food particles, capsules and traces of Celphos, a pesticide.

Naresh further told the court that he subsequently decided to dismember her body. He said he initially attempted to separate the lower part of her body, including her legs, before moving her remains to the bathroom. However, he claimed that he felt physically weak and stopped the process on the first day.

He also described how he used a baby-changing station to block the bedroom doorway before returning to care for their young daughter. He testified that he fed and put the child to sleep but could not sleep himself that night because he was frightened. He also said he avoided going into the prayer room.

Naresh is facing charges including first-degree murder, concealing a body and unlawfully dismembering a human body. Despite his admission about dismembering Mamta's remains, her body has never been recovered.

How the Investigation Began

The investigation started after Mamta, who worked as a nurse at UVA Health Prince William Medical Center in Virginia, failed to show up for work.

Initially, Naresh denied that anything had happened to his wife and reportedly told investigators that he had last seen her on July 29, 2024. However, Mamta's friends and family raised concerns, insisting that she would never voluntarily abandon her young daughter.

Naresh did not report Mamta missing to police until August 5, 2024. During the process, he claimed that she had threatened to leave him and had discussed divorce.

Investigators later discovered blood evidence inside the couple's master bedroom and bathroom. Police also recovered an electric saw with strands of hair caught in it.

Following the discovery of the evidence, Naresh was arrested on August 22, 2024, and has remained in custody since then.

Mamta's Body Has Never Been Found

One of the most disturbing aspects of the case is that investigators have still not recovered Mamta's remains.

Her disappearance shocked Nepal's community in the United States and drew widespread attention from Nepalis at home and abroad. Mamta was a healthcare professional and a mother of a young daughter when she disappeared.

The latest courtroom testimony has brought new details to light about what Naresh claims happened inside their home. However, the circumstances surrounding Mamta's death and the full sequence of events remain central issues in the ongoing murder proceedings.

The case continues to attract attention as the court examines the evidence and Naresh's statements in an effort to establish what happened to Mamta Kafle Bhatt.

Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed took aim at President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance during his victory speech after defeating Trump-backed Republican candidate Mike Rogers in the 2026 US midterm elections. Addressing Vance, El-Sayed jokingly called it “delicious irony” that the vice president would be constitutionally required to swear him into office in January.

“JD, habibi, there is this delicious irony in the fact that you’re constitutionally obligated to swear me in in January,” El-Sayed told supporters in Detroit. He also joked about the sporting rivalry between the University of Michigan and Ohio State University, Vance’s alma mater, saying, “Wolverines 1, Buckeyes 0.”

El-Sayed also responded to Trump, who repeatedly mocked his name and criticised his Muslim faith during the campaign. “Donald, I know you struggle with my name, so after JD swears me in in January, you can go on and call me senator,” he said. El-Sayed, a former Wayne County health director, is set to succeed retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters, keeping the Michigan Senate seat in Democratic hands. According to the report, his election makes him the first Muslim elected to the US Senate.

Three Nepali-origin Americans have reportedly won seats in state legislatures across the United States following the 2026 midterm elections. The winners are Sarahana Shrestha in New York, Dr. Harry Bhandari in Maryland and Bishwabahadur Shah in New Hampshire.

Sarahana Shrestha has secured a third consecutive term representing New York State Assembly District 103. First elected in 2022, she is the first Nepali American to serve in the New York State Legislature and the first Nepali American woman elected to a US state legislature. Her new term is scheduled to begin on January 1, 2027.

In Maryland, Dr. Harry Bhandari has won a third term in the House of Delegates, representing District 8. He first entered the state legislature in 2018 and became the first Nepali American elected to Maryland's legislature. Meanwhile, Bishwabahadur Shah, a Manchester resident, has won a seat in the New Hampshire House of Representatives, representing District 41 in Hillsborough County.

The victories highlight the growing political participation and public representation of the Nepali-origin community in the United States. Their election to legislative positions in three different states marks a notable moment for Nepali Americans and the wider diaspora.

Naresh Bhatt, who is facing murder charges in connection with the disappearance of his wife, Nepali nurse Mamta Kafle Bhatt, has denied physically abusing her while testifying in a Virginia court. However, the 39-year-old acknowledged that their marriage had deteriorated and admitted that he had caused her emotional and mental distress. His testimony came on November 4, the 16th day of the trial, after prosecutors completed presenting their evidence.

During questioning, prosecutor Tracy Lennox confronted Bhatt with text messages exchanged between the couple in the months before Mamta disappeared. Bhatt denied threatening her with physical violence but admitted to emotional mistreatment. He said arguments had become frequent from early 2024, with him threatening divorce and Mamta sometimes threatening suicide. He also acknowledged refusing to eat food she prepared and sometimes stopping communication with her. Democrats Take Control of Congress, Putting Trump Under Pressure as Iran War, Ukraine Aid and Immigration Policies Face New Challenges

KATHMANDU — Democrats have won control of both chambers of the U.S. Congress, delivering a major political setback to President Donald Trump and creating new challenges for his administration. The Democratic Party's victory in the November 3 midterm elections means Republicans have lost their majority in both the Senate and the House of Representatives. The result will make it harder for Trump to pass new laws and carry out his political agenda during the final two years of his presidency.

The election results reflect growing frustration among American voters over rising living costs, trade policies, immigration restrictions and the war with Iran. Democrats gained several seats in traditionally Republican states and districts, showing that many voters wanted stronger checks on Trump's administration. The victory also gives Democrats greater power to investigate the government, question officials and challenge presidential decisions.

What Does the Democratic Victory Mean for Trump?

The U.S. president has broad powers over foreign policy, national security, trade and immigration. However, Congress plays an important role in checking presidential authority. It approves government spending, passes national laws, investigates government activities and reviews many senior appointments.

With Democrats controlling both chambers, Trump will face stronger opposition when trying to pass new laws or secure funding for his policies. Democratic lawmakers will also lead important congressional committees, giving them greater power to investigate decisions made by the Trump administration.

However, the election result does not mean Trump has lost his presidential powers. He can still issue executive orders and make many decisions on trade, immigration and foreign policy without getting approval from Congress. Democrats can hold hearings, question government officials and challenge his decisions, but they cannot automatically cancel every policy introduced by the president.

The new Congress is expected to begin its work in January 2027. Until then, Republicans will continue to control both chambers, meaning the immediate balance of power in Washington will not change overnight.

Can Democrats Stop Trump's Trade Policies?

Trump's trade policies, especially his decision to impose high tariffs on goods from other countries, have been a major source of disagreement between Republicans and Democrats.

Trump has introduced heavy import taxes on products from both rival nations and long-standing U.S. allies, including Canada. He has argued that tariffs protect American industries and help strengthen the country's economy. However, critics say these policies increase costs for businesses and consumers.

Democrats have repeatedly criticized the tariffs but have struggled to challenge them because Republicans controlled Congress. Their new majority will give them more opportunities to question the administration's trade decisions and examine the economic impact of the tariffs.

However, Trump still has significant authority to impose tariffs through existing trade laws. According to James Smith, a market economist at Dutch bank ING, trade is one area where a president can take action without always needing congressional approval.

Democrats may use public hearings, investigations and other political tools to put pressure on the administration. But ending Trump's existing tariff policies will not be easy.

What Happens to Trump's Immigration Policies?

Immigration is another major issue that could create serious disagreements between Trump and the new Democratic Congress.

Trump has repeatedly defended his strict immigration policies, saying stronger border security is necessary to protect the United States and its citizens. His administration has introduced tougher measures targeting illegal immigration and border crossings.

Democrats have strongly criticized several of these policies, arguing that immigration enforcement should protect human rights and provide fair treatment to migrants.

With control of both chambers, Democrats will have more power to investigate immigration enforcement, question officials and challenge new government proposals. They could also use congressional hearings to examine how immigration laws are being implemented.

However, policies that are already in place will not automatically end because Democrats have won the election. Trump can continue using his executive powers, although new legislation and government funding decisions could become more difficult for his administration.

Can Congress Stop Trump From Going to War?

The war with Iran is expected to become one of the biggest sources of conflict between Trump and the new Democratic Congress.

Democratic lawmakers have repeatedly opposed the administration's military actions against Iran and have questioned whether Trump has sufficient legal authority to continue the conflict without congressional approval.

They have previously introduced three War Powers Resolution measures aimed at limiting Trump's military actions. One proposal passed the House of Representatives with support from some Republicans but failed to gain enough votes in the Senate.

Under the U.S. War Powers Resolution, the president must generally notify Congress within 48 hours of introducing U.S. forces into hostilities. Military action is generally limited to 60 days without congressional authorization, with a possible additional 30-day period for withdrawing forces.

Trump has argued that the military operation against Iran does not amount to a formal war. His administration has used this position to defend its actions without seeking a formal declaration of war from Congress.

Democrats could now increase pressure through investigations, hearings and legislation aimed at limiting military operations. They may also demand greater transparency about the cost, goals and legal basis of the conflict.

However, controlling Congress does not automatically give Democrats the power to stop every military action. The president remains commander in chief, and any major effort to restrict his authority could lead to a serious legal and political battle.

Could U.S. Policy Toward Iran Change?

The election result could also influence Trump's next decisions on Iran.

During the campaign, Trump suggested that the United States could take stronger military action against Iran after the election. However, he has also indicated that negotiations could offer a way to end the conflict.

Democrats have generally opposed expanding the war and have called for greater congressional oversight of military decisions.

Following the election results, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed that American voters had rejected the war against Iran. He said the Iranian government supported the American public's opposition to the conflict and warned that ignoring public opinion could have serious consequences for the United States.

Trump has not announced a major change in his Iran policy following the election. However, the new Democratic majority could make it politically more difficult for his administration to continue military operations without facing strong opposition in Congress.

Will America Resume Military Aid to Ukraine?

U.S. support for Ukraine could also become an important issue under the new congressional majority.

Trump recently halted some American assistance to Ukraine, saying he wants to end the war through negotiations between Russia and Ukraine. His administration has supported efforts to bring the two countries to the negotiating table, including talks expected to take place in Abu Dhabi.

Democrats, however, have generally supported continued military and financial assistance to Ukraine as it defends itself against Russia's invasion.

They have also criticized Trump's approach to negotiations, arguing that Ukraine should not be pressured into accepting an unfair agreement that benefits Russia.

With Democrats controlling both chambers, there could be renewed efforts to approve financial and military assistance for Kyiv. Democratic lawmakers may also use congressional oversight to question the administration's decisions on Ukraine.

The change in Congress could therefore offer Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy greater support in Washington. However, any major change in U.S. policy will depend on negotiations between Congress and the White House, as well as the availability of funding.

Can Democrats Remove Trump From Power?

Although Democrats have won control of Congress, the election does not automatically threaten Trump's position as president.

The president cannot be removed simply because his party loses its majority in the midterm elections. Congress can investigate the administration and begin impeachment proceedings if there are sufficient legal and political grounds. Removing a president through impeachment requires a two-thirds majority in the Senate to convict and remove him from office.

Democrats will not have enough votes to achieve that on their own.

They also cannot easily override a presidential veto. If Trump rejects a bill passed by Congress, lawmakers need a two-thirds majority in both the House and Senate to override his decision.

This means Trump will retain important powers even after Democrats take control of Congress. However, his ability to pass new laws and secure support for his policies will face much stronger resistance.

Trump Promises to Work With Democrats

Following the election results, Trump said he was willing to accept the outcome and work with Democrats. He congratulated the opposition party on its victory but rejected the idea that the result was a personal defeat.

Trump also indicated that he could use his presidential veto to block legislation he disagrees with. His comments suggest that cooperation between the White House and Congress may be difficult, especially on major issues such as immigration, trade and foreign policy.

Former President Barack Obama also responded to the election results on social media, saying the outcome could change the country's political direction. He criticized Trump's policies and said American voters wanted political leadership that brought people together rather than divided society.

The Democratic victory marks a major shift in Washington's political balance. Although Trump will remain president and retain significant executive powers, he will now face a Congress controlled by his political opponents. The coming months could bring intense battles over Iran, Ukraine, immigration, trade and government spending as Democrats seek to increase oversight of his administration.

Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has defeated Republican Mike Rogers in Michigan’s U.S. Senate race, making history as the first Muslim elected to the United States Senate. The 42-year-old progressive politician is a former public health official and a strong supporter of universal health care. However, his election victory does not mean he takes office immediately. He will join the Senate when his term officially begins.

Born and raised in southeastern Michigan, El-Sayed is the son of an Egyptian immigrant father. He studied at the University of Michigan, Oxford University, and Columbia University, where he earned degrees in public health and medicine. He previously served as director of the Detroit Health Department and later led the Wayne County Department of Health, Human Services, and Veterans Affairs. His political priorities include affordable health care, reducing living costs, and limiting the influence of wealthy donors in politics.

El-Sayed has clearly supported Ukraine in its war against Russia. Shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, he described the attack as an act of aggression against a democratic country. He praised countries that supported Ukraine by providing weapons and helping refugees. In an August 2026 interview with NBC's Meet the Press, he explained that Ukraine has the right to defend itself against an invasion by another country. He said supporting Ukraine is important for protecting international law and national independence.

His position on Israel is very different. El-Sayed has called for an immediate end to all U.S. military aid to Israel, including both offensive and defensive weapons. He has also supported restoring humanitarian funding for Palestinians, including support for UNRWA, the United Nations agency that helps Palestinian refugees. He has accused Israel of committing genocide in Gaza. His position has created strong disagreements among voters, particularly within Michigan's Jewish community.

However, El-Sayed has said that both Palestinians and Israelis have the right to live in peace, dignity, and security. In a November 1, 2026, interview with 60 Minutes, he said Palestine has a right to exist. He also said Israel has a right to exist, while adding that both sides must agree on a fair political arrangement. He supports either a two-state solution or a single shared state if both communities freely choose that arrangement.

El-Sayed has also faced criticism over his comments about Hamas and an attack on a synagogue in Michigan. In October 2025, his campaign sent a fundraising email criticizing Israel's military actions in Gaza without mentioning Hamas's October 7, 2023, attack on Israel. The email drew criticism, although his campaign said it had been sent by mistake. A separate statement released by El-Sayed on the same day condemned Hamas's attack, the killings, and the taking of hostages.

In March 2026, after an attack on Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield, Michigan, El-Sayed condemned the violence and expressed support for the Jewish community. However, his later comments connecting the attack to the wider Middle East conflict angered some members of the community. In August, he apologized for those remarks, saying his initial condemnation should have been enough. He also stated that antisemitism must be opposed in all its forms.

El-Sayed's election has brought renewed attention to his foreign policy views, especially his different positions on Ukraine and Israel. He argues that supporting Ukraine is necessary because Russia invaded a sovereign country, while he opposes U.S. military support for Israel because of its actions in Gaza. However, his campaign statements do not guarantee how he will vote on every foreign aid proposal. His actual decisions on military assistance, funding, and foreign policy will become clearer after he officially takes his seat in the U.S. Senate.

नेपाली कांग्रेसले पार्टी र नेतृत्वविरुद्ध भइरहेको भनिएको षड्यन्त्र, दुष्प्रचार तथा राज्य संयन्त्रको दुरुपयोगविरुद्ध राजनीतिक र कानुनी रूपमा प्रतिवाद गर्ने जनाएको छ। महामन्त्री प्रदीप पौडेलले मंगलबार सार्वजनिक गरेको ६ बुँदे धारणामार्फत पार्टीको वैधानिकतामाथि उठाइएका प्रश्न र विभिन्न प्रचार निराधार तथा नियोजित भएको दाबी गरेका छन्।

कांग्रेसले २०८२ पुसमा सम्पन्न विशेष महाधिवेशन निर्वाचन आयोगबाट अद्यावधिक भइसकेको र सर्वोच्च अदालतबाट समेत वैधानिक ठहर भएको उल्लेख गरेको छ। साथै, २०८३ असोज १६ देखि २३ गतेसम्म १५औँ महाधिवेशन सम्पन्न भइसकेकाले पार्टीको वैधानिकतामाथि प्रश्न उठाउने प्रयास स्वीकार्य नहुने जनाएको छ।

वरिष्ठ उपसभापति विश्वप्रकाश शर्माले बुधबार पत्रकार सम्मेलन गर्दै पार्टी र नेतृत्वविरुद्ध उठेका प्रश्न तथा छानबिनको सामना गर्न तयार रहेको बताए। उनले इनम सापकोटा प्रकरणमा प्रधानमन्त्री कार्यालयसँग सम्बन्धित व्यक्तिहरूको संलग्नतामा अनुसन्धानमा रहेका व्यक्ति र प्रमाणमाथि अनधिकृत नियन्त्रण तथा छेडछाड भएको भनिएका विषयको निष्पक्ष अनुसन्धान हुनुपर्ने माग गरे।

कांग्रेसले प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक हटाउने घटनालाई पनि यही घटनाक्रमसँग जोड्दै राज्य संयन्त्रको दुरुपयोग भएको आरोप लगाएको छ। पत्रकारमाथिको धरपकड, प्रेस नियन्त्रण र संवैधानिक निकायमाथिको हस्तक्षेपप्रति आपत्ति जनाउँदै पार्टीले कानुनी परामर्श र संसदीय पहल अघि बढाउने जनाएको छ।

कांग्रेसले सरकारलाई प्रतिपक्षलाई कमजोर बनाउने गतिविधि बन्द गरी विपद् प्रभावितको राहत, अर्थतन्त्रको पुनरुत्थान र जनसरोकारका विषयमा ध्यान दिन आग्रह गरेको छ।

प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक (आईजीपी) डा. मनोज केसीले दर्ज्यानी चिह्न लगाएका छन्। बुधबार गृह मन्त्रालयमा गृहमन्त्री सुधन गुरुङले उनलाई दर्ज्यानी चिह्न लगाइदिएका हुन्।

केसी बुधबार नै नेपाल प्रहरीको ३४औँ महानिरीक्षकमा नियुक्त भएका थिए। यसअघि आईजीपीलाई गृहसचिवले दर्ज्यानी चिह्न लगाइदिने परम्परा रहे पनि यसपटक गृहमन्त्री आफैँले चिह्न प्रदान गरेका छन्।

The Nepal Tourism Board has announced its first-ever Kukur Tihar Reel Competition 2026, offering a cash prize of Rs. 1 lakh to the winning creator. The competition aims to promote Nepal’s unique Kukur Tihar festival internationally through creative short videos highlighting the cultural significance of the festival and the special bond between humans and dogs.

To participate, creators must publish an original reel publicly on Instagram or Facebook using the hashtags #NepalFestival and #KukurTihar, while tagging the Nepal Tourism Board on the respective platform. The video must be in English or include English subtitles or an English voice-over.

Participants must also email their video to the Tourism Board with an accessible Google Drive link. The submission deadline is November 21, 2026. According to the Board, submitted reels may also be used for tourism promotion and digital communication.

The competition offers content creators an opportunity to showcase Nepal’s cultural traditions to an international audience while competing for a cash prize of Rs. 100,000.

A Saudi-based company has agreed to pay 181,000 Saudi riyals to the family of Bharat Mahato, a 45-year-old Nepali worker from Mahottari who was killed in a drone attack in Saudi Arabia. The amount includes 31,000 riyals in end-of-service benefits and 150,000 riyals in compensation.

The agreement was reached following an initiative by the Nepali Embassy in Riyadh. According to Nepali Labour Counsellor Kabiraj Upreti, the money will be sent to Bharat’s family after the necessary administrative procedures are completed. The company agreed to provide the compensation on humanitarian grounds after learning that Bharat’s labour permit had expired, potentially making his family ineligible for financial assistance from Nepal’s Foreign Employment Board and insurance.

Bharat had worked for the company for 14 years and was employed at an oil project operated by Saudi Aramco. He was killed on Kartik 4 in a drone attack targeting the Shaybah oil field in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Province. The attack, attributed to Yemen’s Houthi rebels, also killed a Filipino worker.

Bharat was the main financial support for his family and had been building a house near his hometown. His wife is now facing the responsibility of raising their four children while dealing with an outstanding bank loan. Although the Nepali Embassy has completed the necessary procedures to bring his body home, flight disruptions have delayed its return, and the arrival date remains uncertain.

सरकारका प्रवक्ता एवं शिक्षामन्त्री सस्मित पोखरेलले नेपाल प्रहरीका प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक (आईजीपी) दानबहादुर कार्कीको जिम्मेवारी हेरफेर पार्टीको निर्देशनपछि गरिएको बताएका छन्।

बुधबार बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकपछि सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै मन्त्री पोखरेलले बदलिँदो परिस्थितिका कारण पार्टीबाट सरकारलाई संवेदनशील विषयमा आवश्यक कदम चाल्न निर्देशन आएको बताएका हुन्।

‘धेरै ठाउँबाट अहिले बदलिँदो परिस्थिति छ । पार्टीबाट पनि संवेदनशील विषयमा सरकारले केही गर्नुपर्‍यो भनेर निर्देशन आएको थियो,’ मन्त्री पोखरेलले भने, ‘त्यसपछि जिम्मेवारी हेरफेर गरिएको हो।’

उनले प्रधानमन्त्रीलाई शान्ति सुरक्षासम्बन्धी सल्लाह दिने जिम्मेवारी पनि निकै संवेदनशील हुने उल्लेख गरे। यस्तो जिम्मेवारीको महत्वलाई ध्यानमा राखेर निर्णय गरिएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

सरकारको यो अभिव्यक्तिले नेपाल प्रहरीको नेतृत्व परिवर्तनमा पार्टीको निर्देशनले भूमिका खेलेको विषयलाई थप चर्चामा ल्याएको छ।

ईजीपीबाट हटाइए दानबहादुर कार्की, मनोज केसीलाई दिइयो जिम्मेवारी!

नेपाल प्रहरीको नेतृत्व परिवर्तनलाई लिएर राजनीतिक तथा सुरक्षा वृत्तमा चर्चा चर्किएको छ। प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक (आईजीपी) दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई पदबाट हटाएर अतिरिक्त प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक (एआईजी) डा. मनोजकुमार केसीलाई जिम्मेवारी दिइएको दाबी सार्वजनिक भए पनि यसको आधिकारिक पुष्टि हुन सकेको छैन।

पछिल्ला दिनमा सरकार र प्रहरी नेतृत्वबीच मतभेद देखिएको भन्ने समाचार सार्वजनिक भएपछि आईजीपी परिवर्तनको चर्चा सुरु भएको थियो। कार्कीलाई हटाउने तयारी भइरहेको विवरण आएपछि प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयमा उच्च अधिकारीहरूको आकस्मिक बैठकसमेत बसेको थियो।

अक्टोबर २९ मा काठमाडौंको नक्सालस्थित प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयमा बसेको बैठक करिब पाँच घण्टा चलेको थियो। उक्त बैठकमा प्रहरी संगठनको व्यावसायिकता, नेतृत्वमाथि भइरहेको चर्चा र संगठनभित्रको अवस्थाबारे छलफल भएको समाचार प्रकाशित भएको थियो।

राजीनामाको समाचार प्रहरीद्वारा खण्डन

आईजीपी कार्कीले आफूलाई सरकारले राजीनामा दिन भनेको भन्ने विवरण असत्य रहेको बताएका थिए। नेपाल प्रहरी प्रधान कार्यालयले पनि उनको राजीनामासम्बन्धी समाचार भ्रामक भएको भन्दै खण्डन गरेको थियो।

यसैबीच, एआईजी डा. मनोजकुमार केसीको नाम नयाँ प्रहरी प्रमुखका सम्भावित उम्मेदवारका रूपमा चर्चामा आएको छ। केसी नेपाल प्रहरीका अनुभवी अधिकारी हुन्। उनले केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्युरोलगायत विभिन्न महत्त्वपूर्ण जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेका छन्।

नक्कली भुटानी शरणार्थी प्रकरणको अनुसन्धानमा भूमिका निर्वाह गरेका कारण केसी सार्वजनिक चर्चामा आएका प्रहरी अधिकारीमध्ये एक हुन्।

प्रहरी नेतृत्व परिवर्तनमा सरकारको निर्णय महत्त्वपूर्ण

प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकको नियुक्ति तथा पदबाट हटाउने विषय कानुनी प्रक्रियासँग सम्बन्धित हुन्छ। यसका लागि सरकारको औपचारिक निर्णय आवश्यक पर्छ।

हाल नेपाल प्रहरीको आधिकारिक वेबसाइटमा दानबहादुर कार्कीलाई नै प्रहरी महानिरीक्षकका रूपमा उल्लेख गरिएको छ। मनोजकुमार केसीलाई नयाँ आईजीपी नियुक्त गरिएको पुष्टि हुने सरकारी निर्णय उपलब्ध भएको छैन।

प्रहरी नेतृत्व परिवर्तनको चर्चा चर्किए पनि औपचारिक निर्णय नभएसम्म कार्की पदबाट हटेको वा केसीले नयाँ जिम्मेवारी सम्हालिसकेको भन्न मिल्दैन।

यसरी नेपाल प्रहरीको नेतृत्व परिवर्तनबारे व्यापक चर्चा भइरहेका बेला अब सरकारको आधिकारिक निर्णयले मात्रै नयाँ प्रहरी महानिरीक्षक को हुने भन्ने विषय स्पष्ट पार्नेछ।

बागलुङमा राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टी (रास्वपा) का स्थानीय नेता अमर खड्काको घरमा जुवा खेलिरहेको अवस्थामा प्रहरीले ९ जनालाई पक्राउ गरेको छ।

गोप्य सूचनाका आधारमा प्रहरीले छापा मार्दा खड्कासहित ९ जना तास खेलिरहेको अवस्थामा भेटिएको रातोपाटीले जनाएको छ। उनीहरूको साथबाट १ लाख ६४ हजार ९२५ रुपैयाँ नगद बरामद भएको छ।

पक्राउ पर्नेमा बागलुङ नगरपालिका–२ का चिरञ्जीवी शर्मा, रिपोर्ट जिसी, दुर्गाबहादुर खत्री, हरि शर्मा र भीमबहादुर खत्री छन्। त्यस्तै डम्मरबहादुर भण्डारी, राजु गौतम र केशव पराजुली पनि पक्राउ परेका छन्।

प्रहरीका अनुसार पक्राउ परेकाहरूमा नेता, वकिल र स्वास्थ्यकर्मीसमेत रहेका छन्। उनीहरूमाथि थप अनुसन्धान भइरहेको छ।

खड्का यसअघि नेपाली कांग्रेसमा आबद्ध थिए। प्रतिनिधिसभा निर्वाचनअघि उनी रास्वपा प्रवेश गरेका थिए। उनी बागलुङ नगरपालिकाका पार्टी वडासभापति हुन्।

समाचार कक्षभित्रै प्रवेश गरेर पत्रकारमाथि गरिएको प्रहरी धरपकडबारे सरकारले आफूलाई पूर्वजानकारी नभएको स्पष्टीकरण दिएको छ। सरकारका प्रवक्ता सस्मित पोखरेलले उक्त कार्य प्रहरीको आन्तरिक अनुसन्धानका लागि भएको र सरकार वा प्रधानमन्त्रीबाट अनुमति नलिइएको बताएका छन्।

१७ कात्तिकमा सिंहदरबारमा मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकपछि सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै पोखरेलले प्रहरीको आन्तरिक सूचना चुहावटबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न पत्रकारसँग सोधपुछ गरिएको दाबी गरे। प्रधानमन्त्रीले आईजीपीको राजीनामा मागेको वा कारबाही गर्न लागेको भन्ने भ्रामक सूचना कहाँबाट आयो भन्ने विषयमा प्रहरीले तथ्य बुझ्न खोजेको उनको भनाइ थियो।

पोखरेलका अनुसार समाचार प्रकाशित हुने प्रक्रियाबारे बुझ्न प्रहरीले आफ्नै तवरबाट सोधपुछ गरेको हो। यसमा सरकारसँग पूर्ण अनुमति लिइएको थिएन र प्रधानमन्त्री बालेन शाहलाई पनि यसबारे पूर्वजानकारी थिएन।

उनले घटनाबारे जानकारी पाएपछि प्रधानमन्त्रीले कुनै पनि पत्रकारलाई सोधपुछका नाममा हिरासतमा नराख्न निर्देशन दिएको बताए। साथै, पत्रकारलाई गिरफ्तार वा नियन्त्रणमा लिइएको नभई सोधपुछ मात्रै गरिएको सरकारको दाबी छ।

बिचौलिया इनम सापकोटासँगको सम्बन्धका कारण विवादमा परेका सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीश हरिप्रसाद फुयालमाथि अन्य न्यायाधीशहरूले फुलकोर्ट बैठकमै आक्रोश व्यक्त गरेका छन्। सिंगो न्यायालयलाई विवादमा तानेको भन्दै उनीहरूले फुयाललाई ‘तपाईं मात्र विचलित हुनुभएन, हामी सबैलाई डुबाउनुभयो’ भनेको स्रोतको भनाइ छ।

शुक्रबार र आइतबार बसेको पूर्ण बैठकमा न्यायाधीशहरूले होटेल हिमालयमा सापकोटासँग भेट्न गएका अन्य न्यायाधीशहरूको नाम सार्वजनिक गर्न फुयालसँग माग गरेका थिए। केही व्यक्तिको गलत आचरणको भार सिंगो न्यायालयले बोक्न नसक्ने उनीहरूको भनाइ थियो। फुयालले भने आफूले केही गल्ती स्वीकार गर्दै आन्तरिक छानबिन गर्न प्रस्ताव गरेको बताइएको छ।

फुयालले आफ्नो विषय संसदीय छानबिनमा गए धेरै कुरा बाहिर आउन सक्ने र सबैलाई अप्ठ्यारो पर्न सक्ने भन्दै आन्तरिक छानबिनलाई उचित विकल्पका रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेका थिए। उनले छानबिन भए होटेल हिमालयमा गएका अन्य व्यक्तिको नामसमेत खुलाउन सक्ने बताएका थिए। तर, सर्वोच्चको पूर्ण बैठकले आन्तरिक छानबिन समिति गठन नगरी संसदीय छानबिनमार्फत सत्यतथ्य बाहिर ल्याउनुपर्ने संकेत गरेको छ।

बैठकमा सापकोटासँगको सम्पर्कबारे प्रधानन्यायाधीश मनोजकुमार शर्मालाई जानकारी नगराएको विषयमा पनि फुयालसँग प्रश्न गरिएको थियो। साथै, आफूले चिनेको र आफूसँग सम्बन्ध जोडिएको व्यक्तिको बन्दी प्रत्यक्षीकरण मुद्दा आफैँले हेरेको तथा त्यसको फैसलाबारे सार्वजनिक रूपमा बोलेको विषयमा समेत उनको आलोचना भएको थियो।

सापकोटासँगको ह्वाट्सएप कुराकानी सार्वजनिक भएपछि फुयालले उनीसँग भेटेको स्वीकार गरेका थिए। महाअभियोगको त्रासका कारण भेटेको र कुनै गलत नियत नरहेको उनको दाबी छ। यसैबीच, नेपाल बार एसोसिएसनले घटनाको अध्ययन गर्न पूर्वअध्यक्ष चण्डेश्वर श्रेष्ठको नेतृत्वमा ६ सदस्यीय समिति गठन गरेको छ। फुयालले कात्तिक २० गतेसम्म बिदा लिएका छन्।

सत्तारूढ राष्ट्रिय स्वतन्त्र पार्टीले यस प्रकरणमा संसदीय छानबिन गर्ने निर्णय गरिसकेको छ भने सर्वोच्चको पूर्ण बैठकले पनि संसदीय छानबिनबाट सत्यतथ्य बाहिर ल्याउन आग्रह गरेको छ।

राष्ट्रिय प्रजातन्त्र पार्टी (राप्रपा) की प्रमुख सचेतक खुश्बु ओलीले एकदुई जना न्यायाधीशमाथि महाभियोग लगाउँदैमा न्यायालयमा देखिएका विकृति र विसंगति अन्त्य नहुने बताएकी छन्। उनले न्यायालय सुधारका लागि समग्र पुनःसंरचना आवश्यक रहेको भन्दै सरकारलाई यस विषयमा गम्भीर बन्न आग्रह गरेकी छन्।

सोमबार नेपाली कांग्रेसको आह्वानमा सिंहदरबारमा बसेको प्रतिपक्षी दलहरूको बैठकपछि सञ्चारकर्मीसँग कुरा गर्दै ओलीले न्यायालयको विषयलाई संसद्मा गम्भीर बहसको विषय बनाउनुपर्ने बताइन्।

सर्वोच्च अदालतका न्यायाधीशदेखि प्रधानन्यायाधीशसम्मको नाम जोडेर विभिन्न घटना सार्वजनिक भइरहँदा न्यायालयप्रति सर्वसाधारणको विश्वास कमजोर हुँदै गएको उनको भनाइ थियो।

‘एकदुई जना व्यक्तिमाथि महाभियोग लगाउँदैमा न्यायालयको समग्र सुधार सम्भव हुँदैन,’ उनले भनिन्, ‘न्यायालयको पुनःसंरचनामा सरकार गम्भीर हुनुपर्छ। न्यायालयको विषयलाई संसद्मा गम्भीर बहसमा लैजान यथाशीघ्र संसद् आह्वान गर्नुपर्छ।’

ओलीले न्यायालयमा देखिएका समस्या समाधानका लागि सीमित व्यक्तिमाथिको कारबाहीभन्दा पनि संस्थागत सुधारमा ध्यान दिनुपर्ने धारणा राखिन्।

उनले न्यायालयको विषयसँगै प्रहरी र सरकारबीचको सम्बन्ध तथा अर्थमन्त्री स्वर्णिम वाग्लेले भारतमा दिएको अभिव्यक्तिबारे पनि संसद्मा छलफल हुनुपर्ने बताइन्।

प्रतिपक्षी दलहरूको बैठकले सरकारसँग जोडिएका विभिन्न विषय संसद्मा उठाउनुपर्ने धारणा राखिरहेका बेला राप्रपाले पनि तत्काल संसद् अधिवेशन आह्वान गर्न माग गरेको हो।

Melania Trump Hosts Historic White House Summit With Russian And Ukrainian Envoys
First Lady Melania Trump convened high-level representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House, marking an unprecedented diplomatic summit uniting delegates from two actively warring nations in Washington. Documented in an official statement from the White House and covered by CNN Politics, the gathering followed Mrs. Trump's direct involvement as exclusive intermediary in brokering a localized humanitarian ceasefire in the frontline city of Oleshky, which enabled the safe evacuation of nearly 800 civilians.

Key Diplomatic Breakthroughs
Unprecedented Diplomatic Precedent
The meeting represents the first time in American history that a First Lady personally brought together official delegates from two warring foreign nations at the White House to advance direct humanitarian diplomacy.

Ukraine State Honor Conferred
Ukrainian representatives formally presented Mrs. Trump with the Order of Princess Olga, First Class, a state honor bestowed by President Volodymyr Zelensky in recognition of her leadership in establishing the evacuation corridor.

Direct Letters To Putin And Zelensky
Concluding her remarks, Mrs. Trump entrusted the highest-ranking Russian and Ukrainian envoys in attendance with personal letters addressed directly to President Vladimir Putin and President Volodymyr Zelensky urging broader peace talks.

Frontline Humanitarian Relief
The diplomatic framework allowed critical food, clean water, and medical resources to cross contested battle lines in the Kherson region, detailed in international coverage by CBC News.

On November 18, 1952, Navy pilot Royce Williams took off from the USS Oriskany and flew into history. Alone over the Sea of Japan, he was jumped by seven Soviet MiG-15s — and fought them all, for thirty-five minutes, shooting down four and crippling the attack before his shot-up Panther limped home.

The mission was classified for decades because the Soviets weren't supposed to be there. Williams couldn't tell his story for fifty years. In 2023, at age ninety-seven, he finally received the Navy Cross.

One pilot. Seven MiGs. Seventy years of silence. Then the truth.

#RoyceWilliams #KoreanWar #USNavy #NavyCross #NeverForget

Captain Manuel "Pete" Fernandez was the third-ranking American ace of the Korean War, with fourteen and a half victories — nearly all of them MiG-15s over MiG Alley in 1952 and 1953. Aggressive, brilliant, and utterly fearless, he once downed four MiGs in a single day.

Like so many Korean War aces, Fernandez never really left the cockpit behind. He stayed in the Air Force, kept flying, kept testing the edge — until a crash in 1980 ended the story.

Fourteen and a half. The half counts. Every one of them was earned the hard way.

#ManuelFernandez #KoreanWar #FlyingAce #USAF #MiGAlley

More than fifteen years after Operation Neptune Spear, the heavily modified stealth Black Hawks that carried U.S. Navy SEALs into Abbottabad, Pakistan, remain among modern aviation’s closest-guarded secrets.

This rare, undated photo—originally analyzed by aviation specialists at The War Zone (TWZ) and discussed across the aviation community—shows a heavily modified EH-60 testbed fitted with low-observable treatments.

Visible modifications include:

A faceted, radar-deflecting nose profile designed to scatter radar returns

An enclosed aerodynamic rotor mast and hub fairing

Cantilevered composite stub wings carrying specialized low-observable external fuel tanks

Shielded engine intakes and infrared-suppressing exhaust baffles

Aviation historians trace this airframe to the U.S. Army's secretive Aviation Technology Office (ATO) formerly known as the Flight Concepts Division (FCD) stationed out of Felker Army Airfield at Fort Eustis, Virginia. ATO is widely recognized as the covert unit that spearheaded development of the modified MH-60 "Ghost Hawks" flown by the 160th SOAR (Night Stalkers) during the 2011 raid.

In April 1951, Captain James Jabara became America's first jet ace — the first pilot to down five enemy jets in the jet age. Flying F-86 Sabres over MiG Alley, the son of Lebanese immigrants dueled Soviet-built MiG-15s in fights that lasted minutes and decided nothing except who went home.

He survived the war's deadliest skies. The aces of Korea wrote the book the next generation flew by.

Captain Joseph McConnell was the top American ace of the Korean War — sixteen MiG-15s downed in four months of flying F-86 Sabres over MiG Alley in early 1953. He did it with a mechanic's precision and a fighter pilot's nerve, in the most demanding air combat of the jet age.

He came home a hero, then went back to the dangerous work he loved: test flying. In August 1954, his F-86H came apart over the California desert, and McConnell — who had survived everything the MiGs could throw at him — was k*lled in a crash.

Sixteen victories in one war. Gone at thirty-two. The sky remembers him.

#JosephMcConnell #KoreanWar #FlyingAce #USAF #NeverForget

He was a stray with no name, found wandering a college campus in 1917. He would become one of the most famous war heroes America ever had, and he was a dog.

Soldiers of the 102nd Infantry were training at Yale when a short, brindle stray with a stubby tail wandered in. A young private, J. Robert Conroy, named him Stubby and smuggled him aboard the troopship to France.

Over 18 months in the trenches, Stubby was present for 17 battles. By the stories told of him, he learned to smell poison gas and would bark to wake sleeping soldiers before it reached them, and he found wounded men in the ground between the trenches. He was even said to have caught a German scout by the seat of his pants, which, as legend has it, earned him the rank of sergeant.

He came home a celebrity, met three presidents, and later became Georgetown's mascot. When he died in 1926, both the New York Times and the Washington Post ran obituaries.

Today, Sergeant Stubby still stands in the Smithsonian.

General Maxwell Taylor commanded the Eighth Army through the Korean War's final grinding year, 1953 — the year of the hill battles, Pork Chop Hill and Old Baldy, where the war's last terrible fighting happened even as peace talks dragged on.

Taylor was a soldier's soldier: a paratrooper who had jumped into Normandy, now directing a static, brutal war of outposts and artillery. He held the line, backed his men, and brought the command home intact when the armistice came.

He would later reshape the entire Army. But in Korea, his job was simpler: hold, and bring them home.

#MaxwellTaylor #KoreanWar #USArmy #EighthArmy #NeverForget

On July 27, 1953, General Mark Clark put his name to the armistice that ended three years of fighting in Korea. It was a strange victory — no parade, no surrender ceremony, just a ceasefire line across a ruined peninsula and millions of lives changed forever.

Clark had commanded the UN forces through the war's grinding final year, holding the line while diplomats argued at Panmunjom. He later said he was the first American commander to sign an armistice without victory — and he carried that weight honestly.

Peace without triumph is still peace. Clark signed it, and the guns went quiet.

#MarkClark #KoreanWar #Armistice #USArmy #NeverForget

In the summer of 1948, American pilot Gail Halvorsen was flying around the clock into West Berlin, which the Soviets had blockaded to try to starve it into surrender. During some time off, he walked to a fence at the edge of the airfield where about 30 children stood watching the planes. They had almost nothing, but they didn't beg. He had only two sticks of gum. He broke them up and passed the pieces through the wire, and the kids who got a piece tore the wrappers so the others could just smell it.

He promised to come back and drop more. How would they know his plane? Watch for the one wiggling its wings.

The next day he dropped chocolate and gum on little handkerchief parachutes, and it grew from there. "Operation Little Vittles" reached 23 tons of candy on more than 250,000 parachutes. The children called him "Uncle Wiggly Wings."

One boy told him the candy wasn't just sweet. "It was hope."

Gail Halvorsen, the Berlin Candy Bomber, died in 2022 at the age of 101.

When North Korea invaded in June 1950, Lieutenant General George Stratemeyer commanded the Far East Air Forces — and in the war's first desperate weeks, his was often the only American power that could reach the battlefield. His bombers and fighters bought the time the ground forces needed to survive.

Stratemeyer built the air campaign from almost nothing: shattered runways, obsolete maps, and an enemy with MiGs. By the time he left in 1951, Allied air power owned the skies over Korea — a dominance that never broke for the rest of the war.

Air wars are won by planners as much as pilots. Stratemeyer was the planner.

They deploy into hostile and austere environments, often alongside other special operations teams, to establish airfields, control aircraft, and bring air power to bear. Their motto sums it up: "First There."

Baker's career in the field goes back years. In 2005, as a Senior Airman with the 21st Special Tactics Squadron at Pope Air Force Base, he was named the Air Force Combat Control Airman of the Year. Among the work recognized that year, he directed the delivery of humanitarian relief supplies to impoverished schools reopening after years of tyrannical oppression.

It's a reminder that the skills Combat Controllers bring to the battlefield don't only deliver firepower. They can also deliver hope.

In September 1965, Lieutenant Colonel Robinson Risner was leading one of the war's boldest air strikes when his F-105 was shot down over North Vietnam. What followed was more than seven years as a POW — years of torture, isolation, and resistance in which Risner, as a senior officer, held his fellow prisoners together.

Before his capture, Risner had already become a legend: a Korean War ace who volunteered for Vietnam and flew some of the most dangerous missions of the air war. In captivity, his courage took a quieter form — refusing to break, keeping faith, leading from inside a cell.

He came home in 1973 with his honor intact and his spirit unbroken. Twice awarded the Air Force Cross, he remains one of the greats of American air power.

After nearly 60 years, the Vietnam-era Hueys that have served the Washington, D.C., area are starting to retire, and their replacement has just arrived.

In an early-November ceremony at Joint Base Andrews, the first of 26 HH-60W Jolly Green II helicopters touched down, flown straight from Sikorsky's plant in Connecticut. It is the first new rotary-wing aircraft to call the D.C. area home in almost six decades.

The upgrade is significant. Compared with the aging UH-1N Huey, the Jolly Green II has a larger airframe, carries far more fuel, flies faster and farther, and offers about three times the airlift capability. And unlike the Hueys' blue, white, and gold paint, the new aircraft will stay gray.

"This mission deserves the modern capability and safety upgrades that are available today," said Col. Karl W. Seekamp, who called the transition a "monumental milestone."

The handover will take years, with full operational capability expected by 2030. But after 60 years, a new chapter has begun.

From 1965 to 1967, Lieutenant General Lewis Walt commanded every Marine in Vietnam — III Marine Amphibious Force — during the hardest years of the buildup. A decorated World War II and Korea veteran, Walt believed the war would be decided in the villages, and he pushed his Marines to protect the population as fiercely as they fought the enemy.

Under his command, the Marines pioneered pacification efforts that became models studied for decades. Walt never pretended the war was simple. He just insisted it be fought with both courage and conscience.

He led the Corps' largest combat command through its trial by fire, and he never asked his Marines to do anything he wouldn't do himself.

While much of Western Europe spent the post-Cold War decades downsizing heavy armor divisions, Poland a nation of 38 million is executing the most ambitious conventional military buildup on the European continent.

By the end of the decade, the Polish Land Forces are projected to field an active arsenal of over 1,500 modern main battle tanks. For comparison, the combined tank fleets of the United Kingdom (~150), France (~220), Germany (~300), and Italy (~200) total fewer than 900 vehicles.

Key pillars behind Poland’s armored juggernaut:

Warsaw has acquired 366 U.S. Abrams tanks, including 250 factory-fresh M1A2 SEPv3 variants and 116 upgraded M1A1 FEP models to anchor heavy mechanized divisions along the eastern border.

A landmark agreement secures 1,000 K2 Black Panther tanks, consisting of 180 initial deliveries and 820 K2PL variants co-produced in Polish factories with localized reactive armor and active protection systems.

 Poland leads the entire NATO alliance in defense investment, dedicating over 4% of its GDP to military procurement and readiness.

The tank buildup is integrated with 96 Boeing AH-64E Apache Guardian attack helicopters, hundreds of HIMARS and K239 Chunmoo rocket launchers, and F-35A Lightning II stealth fighters.

 Poland is actively scaling its armed forces toward a target of 300,000 personnel, cementing its status as NATO’s primary conventional land bulwark on the Eastern Flank.

The center of gravity in European defense has permanently shifted east from the Rhine to the Vistula.

Chief Special Warfare Operator (SEAL) Kevin A. Houston grew up in West Hyannisport, Massachusetts, on Cape Cod, and graduated from Barnstable High School in 1994. He enlisted in the Navy in January 1995 and completed SEAL training in 1999, beginning a career that took him through SEAL Team 4 and eventually to DEVGRU, the Navy's Special Mission Unit.

On August 6, 2011, during his fourth tour in Afghanistan, Houston was aboard the CH-47 Chinook known as Extortion 17 when it was shot down in Wardak Province. The helicopter was carrying a quick reaction force to reinforce Army Rangers already engaged on the ground. All 38 people on board were killed, including 30 Americans, making it the single greatest loss of life in Naval Special Warfare history.

He was 35 years old. Friends remembered him as kind, outgoing, and tougher than anyone around him, and his mother said he was born to be a SEAL. He left behind his wife, Meiling, and their three children.

Lieutenant General Victor "Brute" Krulak saw the Vietnam War more clearly than almost anyone in Washington — and paid the price for saying so. As the Marines' leading counterinsurgency thinker, he argued the war would be won by protecting villages, not by body counts, and he built the Combined Action Program that put Marines to live and fight alongside Vietnamese villagers.

His warnings went unheeded, and the big-unit war ground on. But the Marines who served in the CAP program never forgot what Krulak understood: that the people were the prize, and that winning them mattered more than any statistic.

A warrior and a scholar, in an era that needed both.

THE CAMP PENDLETON GRENADE PIT SACRIFICE  MARINE INSTRUCTOR THREW STUDENT TO SAFETY AND SHIELDED HIM FROM DEADLY BLAST

In an act of instantaneous courage at the School of Infantry-West, Marine combat instructor Staff Sgt. Brett Meil placed his own body directly over a live, ticking M67 fragmentation grenade to shield a panicked recruit, absorbing the blast to save a fellow Marine, as documented by Marines.mil and the USO.

For his extraordinary heroism in the face of death, Meil was awarded the Navy and Marine Corps Medal, the military’s highest non-combat decoration for valor.

The Split-Second Crucible in Pit Two
According to official Marine Corps accounts and reporting by Marine Corps Times, the entire incident unfolded in less than five seconds:

The Freeze Under Pressure: During a live-fire grenade qualification range at Camp Pendleton, California, an entry-level student Marine pulled the pin on an M67 grenade. When the safety lever unexpectedly released in his hand, the student froze in terror with the fuse actively burning.

 Recognizing the imminent catastrophe, Meil stepped directly into the danger zone, forcibly stripped the live munition from the student's locked grip, and physically vaulted both the recruit and himself over the concrete revetment wall.

After hitting the ground outside the bunker, Meil realized the armed grenade had bounced off the ledge and landed within the lethal casualty radius of their prone position. Without hesitation, Meil threw his entire torso over the young Marine to absorb the impact.

Surviving the Blast: The grenade detonated inches away, peppering Meil with dozens of high-velocity shrapnel wounds across his body while leaving his student with only minor injuries. Following emergency surgery, Meil made a complete recovery, resumed his duties training future infantrymen, and was named a 2024 USO Service Member of the Year.

How does Staff Sgt. Brett Meil’s selfless instinct to shield a recruit define the core ethos of the Marine Corps?

On ballots across the country this election, a striking number of names belong to people who have already served their country once, in uniform. According to the nonpartisan nonprofit With Honor Action, 258 military veterans are running for Congress in the 2026 midterms, up 21% from 213 in 2024.

And it isn't a one-party story. Veterans are running across the whole spectrum: 115 Republicans, 80 Democrats, and 63 independents or third-party candidates. In some districts, former service members are even running against each other. This year also sees 38 women veterans on the ballot, up from 21 in 2024.

For decades, the share of veterans in Congress steadily declined. Groups like With Honor exist to reverse that, encouraging veterans of both parties to run, on the idea that people who've served bring a mission-first, work-across-the-aisle instinct. As the group's CEO put it: "Every one of these candidates has already sworn an oath to the Constitution. Congress needs more of it."

They'll win and lose like anyone, and they'll still disagree once in office. But the instinct, to step forward and serve again, is one most people can respect, whatever their politics.

Seconds count when the call comes down—and every piece of kit has its exact place.

A meticulously staged team room gear locker belonging to a DEVGRU (SEAL Team 6) assaulter at an austere Forward Operating Base, prepped for immediate infiltration into the night.

In the world of Tier 1 counter-terrorism, there is no time to rummage through duffels when an assault force spins up. Every inch of gear is dialed in, customized, and staged for rapid staging. On the top shelf sit panoramic ground night vision goggles (GPNVG-18s) alongside staged batteries, infrared beacons, and spare magazines. Below hangs a dialed-in Multicam plate carrier packed with fresh combat mags, dual comms routing, and immediate-access trauma medical gear, centered between a high-cut ballistic helmet and a battle belt configured for secondary weapon retention. Standing ready at the flank is the workhorse: a suppressed assault rifle rigged with thermal/night optics and weapon lights.

Behind the plywood locker walls lies the quiet discipline of Naval Special Warfare. It’s an obsessive attention to detail honed through thousands of hours in shoot-houses, jump schools, and combat rotations—ensuring that when boots hit the deck, the operator and his equipment move as one.

Craftsmanship, lethality, and total readiness.

Ready to strike from the shadows. 🇺🇸🔱⚡🦅

SURROUNDED BY 300 TALIBAN AT COP KEATING, WOUNDED STAFF SGT. RALLIED COUNTERATTACK: CLINTON ROMESHA’S STAND FOR HIS MEN

At dawn on October 3, 2009, roughly 50 American soldiers defending Combat Outpost Keating—a remote, indefensible base situated at the bottom of a steep valley in eastern Afghanistan’s Nuristan Province—woke to a coordinated ambush by more than 300 heavily armed Taliban fighters raining down fire from the surrounding high ground.

During what became known as the Battle of Kamdesh, Section Leader Staff Sgt. Clinton Romesha of Bravo Troop, 3-61 Cavalry, 4th Brigade Combat Team, 4th Infantry Division, orchestrated a legendary defense recognized with the nation's highest military decoration, as documented by the U.S. Army and the Congressional Medal of Honor Society.

Gallantry Under Overwhelming Fire
According to his official Medal of Honor citation, Romesha’s actions prevented the outpost from being completely overrun:

Leading Through the Breach: After shrapnel from an RPG blast wounded his neck, shoulder, and arm, Romesha refused medical evacuation, immediately taking charge of the tactical counter-effort and moving through relentless direct machine-gun fire to rally isolated defenders.

Neutralizing High-Ground Positions: Operating without cover, Romesha utilized an array of weapons—firing an M4 carbine, taking up a fallen comrade’s sniper rifle, and employing an AT4 rocket launcher—to eliminate multiple enemy fighting positions and machine-gun bunkers.

Directing Devastating Close Air Support: Under sustained sniper fire, he calibrated target coordinates for incoming F-15E Strike Eagles, B-1B Lancers, and AH-64 Apache gunships, bringing ordnance dangerously close to friendly positions to decimate advancing Taliban waves.

The Stand for Fallen Brothers: As enemy fighters breached the perimeter, Romesha assembled a volunteer team of five soldiers, leading a push across 100 meters of exposed ground to recover the bodies of fallen teammates and secure the ammunition point so no American was left behind.

Eight American heroes made the ultimate sacrifice that day defending COP Keating: Staff Sgt. Justin Gallegos, Sgt. Christopher Griffin, Sgt. Joshua Kirk, Sgt. Michael Scusa, Spc. Stephan Mace, Spc. Kevin Thomson, Sgt. Vernon Martin, and Sgt. Joshua Hardt.

The United States has struck an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow waterway that acts as a valve for a huge share of the world's oil. A small action in one of the most consequential stretches of water on Earth, and the latest in a quiet standoff between Washington and Tehran that most of the world is barely watching.

The strike hit Qeshm Island, Iran's largest in the Persian Gulf, overnight into November 3. According to US officials cited by the Wall Street Journal, the target was a newly built Iranian anti-aircraft site, and it followed two incidents the day before: an Iranian surface-to-air missile fired at a US jet, which struck back in self-defense, and a US interception of an Iranian missile launched from Qeshm toward commercial shipping. No casualties were reported.

Why does one island matter? The Strait of Hormuz is a chokepoint barely 20 miles wide, and roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through it. By threatening the ships that transit it, Iran can rattle the entire global energy market. Qeshm sits right at the mouth of the strait.

Much remains unconfirmed, and early reports are often incomplete. But the shape of it is clear: the US and Iran remain locked in a dangerous, deliberately restrained standoff over the most important waterway in the global economy.

“OFF-DUTY AT AN OKINAWA GAS STATION, A U.S. MARINE HEARD A CRASH AND SPRANG INTO ACTION.”

On October 15, 2026, U.S. Marine Corps Sergeant Jacob L. Lyons had stopped at a gas station in Uruma, Okinawa, Japan, when the violent sound of a two-vehicle collision shattered the evening quiet.

He didn't hesitate. Sprinting toward the mangled wreckage, the off-duty Explosive Ordnance Disposal (EOD) technician with the 9th Engineer Support Battalion (Combat Logistics Regiment 37, 3rd Marine Logistics Group) found an elderly Japanese woman trapped inside her car, pinned hard against the steering wheel, in severe pain and distress.

What happened next represents the best of the American military community overseas:

Freeing the Trapped Driver: Lyons forced open the passenger-side door and, teaming up with a local Japanese bystander, manually forced the driver's seat rearward to relieve the crushing pressure on her chest and give her room to breathe.

Immediate Trauma Care: Lyons’ wife a former U.S. Navy Corpsman rushed over with another bystander to contact emergency dispatchers, providing immediate first aid and comforting the terrified driver through the language barrier.

Securing the Scene: Recognizing the danger of secondary collisions on the active roadway, Lyons stepped out into traffic, directing vehicles away from the wreckage and maintaining a clear access lane for incoming Japanese police and ambulances.

On October 23, 2026, at Camp Kinser, Colonel Robert Gerbracht presented Sergeant Lyons with the Navy and Marine Corps Achievement Medal for his swift life-saving actions.

“In a moment when another person's well-being was at stake, Sergeant Lyons did not hesitate,” said Col. Gerbracht. “He stepped forward with compassion, calm, and courage to help a member of our Okinawan community in need. His actions are a powerful reflection of our Marine Corps values and of the responsibility we carry as neighbors, partners, and guests in Japan.”

For Lyons, the motivation was simple:

“It was the right thing to do, not just as a Marine, but as a good person. Someone was in need and I was able to help, so I needed to.”

A former Fort Bragg contractor has been arrested and charged with leaking classified special operations material online. James Thomas Ashbacher, 37, of Spring Lake, North Carolina, was arrested by the FBI on October 27. Beginning around 2021, he worked for a private company providing security and emergency management services at a U.S. Army Special Operations Command facility at Fort Bragg, a position that required a Top Secret clearance.

Prosecutors allege that between 2021 and March 2024, Ashbacher photographed and removed classified images and videos of military operations and posted them to social media. When other users reposted the material, he allegedly messaged one of them asking them to "take 'em down, tuck them away, and repost them in a year or two when my contract ends lol."

According to the indictment, a search of his home in April 2025 turned up a classified military award write-up and night vision goggles belonging to an Army special operations unit, valued at around $40,000. He faces charges of unlawfully transmitting and retaining national defense information and theft of government property.

Ashbacher is presumed innocent unless proven guilty. But in a community where operational security keeps people alive, allegations like these hit hard.

OPSEC isn't optional.

More than fifteen years after Operation Neptune Spear, the heavily modified stealth Black Hawks that carried U.S. Navy SEALs into Abbottabad, Pakistan, remain among modern aviation’s closest-guarded secrets.

This rare, undated photo—originally analyzed by aviation specialists at The War Zone (TWZ) and discussed across the aviation community—shows a heavily modified EH-60 testbed fitted with low-observable treatments.

Visible modifications include:

A faceted, radar-deflecting nose profile designed to scatter radar returns

An enclosed aerodynamic rotor mast and hub fairing

Cantilevered composite stub wings carrying specialized low-observable external fuel tanks

Shielded engine intakes and infrared-suppressing exhaust baffles

Aviation historians trace this airframe to the U.S. Army's secretive Aviation Technology Office (ATO) formerly known as the Flight Concepts Division (FCD) stationed out of Felker Army Airfield at Fort Eustis, Virginia. ATO is widely recognized as the covert unit that spearheaded development of the modified MH-60 "Ghost Hawks" flown by the 160th SOAR (Night Stalkers) during the 2011 raid.

U.S. Army Paratrooper Sergeant Markevian Slacks (left), serving with the storied 173rd Airborne Brigade ("Sky Soldiers"), standing alongside a NATO partner soldier in full tactical kit during a joint European training exercise in Italy.

Based out of Vicenza, Italy, the Sky Soldiers serve as America’s rapid-reaction contingency force for Europe and Africa—constantly training in tough field environments, jumping into international drop zones, and standing ready to deploy on a moment’s notice. SGT Slacks answered that call, proudly wearing the airborne wings and carrying the weight of frontline readiness with humility, discipline, and a quiet smile.

Tragically, SGT Slacks lost his life as a result of an off-duty vehicle accident in Italy, cutting short the life of an exceptional young non-commissioned officer who had so much left to give to his family, his squad, and his nation. The pain of an empty chair in the platoon hits just as deep when a soldier is taken on home station.

A proud paratrooper whose commitment, character, and sacrifice will forever be honored by the men and women who stood beside him in formation.

Rest easy, Sergeant Slacks. Sky Soldiers never die—they just slip away into the blue.

On March 16, 1968, helicopter pilot Hugh Thompson Jr. was flying over the village of My Lai when he saw something that stopped him cold: American troops k*lling unarmed Vietnamese civilians. What he did next took more courage than combat.

Thompson landed his OH-23 between the soldiers and the villagers, ordered his crew to train their guns on their fellow Americans if they tried to harm anyone else, and began evacuating the wounded. Then he reported everything he had seen — setting in motion the investigation that exposed the massacre.

The Army tried to bury his story. It took thirty years for Thompson to receive the Soldier's Medal. He never wavered: doing the right thing was the whole point.

On November 18, 1952, Navy pilot Royce Williams took off from the USS Oriskany and flew into history. Alone over the Sea of Japan, he was jumped by seven Soviet MiG-15s — and fought them all, for thirty-five minutes, shooting down four and crippling the attack before his shot-up Panther limped home.

The mission was classified for decades because the Soviets weren't supposed to be there. Williams couldn't tell his story for fifty years. In 2023, at age ninety-seven, he finally received the Navy Cross.

One pilot. Seven MiGs. Seventy years of silence. Then the truth.

Visible modifications include:

A faceted, radar-deflecting nose profile designed to scatter radar returns

An enclosed aerodynamic rotor mast and hub fairing

Cantilevered composite stub wings carrying specialized low-observable external fuel tanks

Shielded engine intakes and infrared-suppressing exhaust baffles
